findings.title: Unbounded multipart uploads are processed by ImageMagick before validation
findings.body: The new resizing path runs for every multipart image over the configured image limit, but there is no upper bound on `tempfile.size` before invoking `OptimizedImage.downsize`. The browser-side 10 MB check is bypassable by posting directly to this endpoint, so an attacker can submit a very large or decompression-bomb image and force up to five expensive ImageMagick conversions before `Upload.create_for` has a chance to reject it. This creates a CPU, memory, and disk denial-of-service path. Enforce a server-side input-size cap before image processing (and reject files above it) rather than relying on the client limit.

findings.title: Image conversion uses the same path as both input and output
findings.body: `OptimizedImage.downsize` is called with `tempfile.path` for both `from` and `to`. The generated `convert`/`gifsicle` command therefore overwrites the source while it is being read; ImageMagick conversion is intended to write to a separate output file (or use a tool explicitly designed for in-place updates). This can cause conversion failures or leave the upload tempfile truncated/corrupted, after which the controller uploads the damaged file or reports an unrelated validation error. Convert into a separate tempfile, check the conversion result and resulting size, then atomically replace the original only on success.

findings.title: Client upload limits no longer honor configured per-type limits
findings.body: The client previously used `max_image_size_kb` or `max_attachment_size_kb` according to `type`; it now always permits up to 10 MB. Sites configured with a smaller limit will let users select files that the server rejects, while sites configured with a larger limit will reject valid uploads in the browser. The matching 413 message is also now inaccurate for servers with non-10-MB limits. Keep the site settings for attachments and the applicable image limit, or introduce and consistently use a documented separate maximum source-image limit for the downsize feature.
